title.narrative: Activity under preparation Contribution Agreement for Pacific Correspondent Banking Relationships (CBR) Multi-Donor Trust Fund

description.narrative: Contract related to: Contribution Agreement for Pacific Correspondent Banking Relationships (CBR) Multi-Donor Trust Fund - The Pacific Island Countries (PICs) are geographically diverse yet face similar economic and financial challenges. PICs are uniquely vulnerable to the withdrawal of Correspondent Banking Relations (CBRs), which underpin vital financial flows such as international trade, remittances, tourism revenues, and humanitarian aid. There are two drivers of CBR withdrawal, known as "de-risking". First, rising risk management and compliance costs related to anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) have contributed to a worldwide contraction in correspondent banking networks. Second -and more relevant for the Pacific- the low volume of transactions in PICs makes CBRs unprofitable for correspondent banks (insufficient economies of scale).The objective of the Action is to strengthen the economic and financial resilience of Pacific Island countries facing the withdrawal of their correspondent banking relationships. This will involve supporting PICs to (i) establish a regional facility for CBR services (or Pacific payment mechanism) that provides a single point of entry for correspondent banks, (ii) promote financial access and interconnectivity through investments in financial infrastructure, and (iii) enhance regional resilience through policy and regulatory reforms, risk assessments, and upstream work.The expected outcomes of the Action are to avoid disruptions in financial flows to and from PICs, improve access to cross-border transactions, increase the resilience of CBRs in PICs, develop enhanced legal and regulatory frameworks, and ensure continuous access to correspondent banking services (with the implementation of the Pacific Payment Mechanism). The achievement of these outcomes will result in lower transaction costs and faster transfers of money for trade, remittances, and development, humanitarian, and disaster relief funds. Ultimately, this contributes to strengthened financial resilience and diversified and sustainable economic growth.The Action contributes to Priority Area 2 "Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Development" of the Pacific chapter under Priority 1 "Regional Integration and Cooperation" of the Regional Multi-annual Indicative Programme Asia and the Pacific 2021-2027 and, in particular, to the Specific Objective: Support diversified, sustainable, and resilient economic growth.
